capabilities: Store one approved plan per project as mozak.json and mozak.md files in the vault
Let agents read plans and propose changes through an MCP server or skill
Require owner approval for plan direction and build start as two separate yeses
Refuse stale writes so concurrent agents cannot overwrite each other
Show all projects' roadmaps, outcomes and progress in a sidebar with a Focus tab
extras: Desktop-only plugin. The mozak CLI, MCP server and skill come from a separate npm package; the Obsidian sidebar is read-only for plans (approvals happen in agent chat). README honestly reports a small pilot found no significant token-use benefit for agents. Linux and macOS only; Windows and network filesystems unsupported.
motivation: The author wanted agents that work in ideas and plans rather than code to share one plan, without repeating project context to each agent or losing work to overwrites.
problem: Coding agents forget project plans between sessions and can overwrite each other's writes, and there is no single Obsidian view of every project's plan and progress.

relations.evidence: Checked so far: jcode (skill and MCP) and Claude Code (MCP).
It works with any agent that can load a skill or an MCP server.

requires.name: Node 24.11+ and Git, plus a coding agent (jcode or Claude Code verified)

summary: Project-plan system that stores one approved plan per project as plain files, lets AI coding agents propose changes, and shows progress in a sidebar.
